title: Making $65 a week at seventeen and reassuring his parents
summary: He earned $65 weekly when working men made $15-18, sent money home and found New York nothing like the warnings.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Do you remember what you were being paid?
Yeah, I remember what I was being paid. I don't know what the rest of them were being paid. I was getting $65 a week.
Which was good money then, wasn't it?

Yeah. The average working man wasn't making but $15 and $18 a week. I mean, the average working man. We was getting sixty-five dollars a week! That's what I was getting, and I'm the last one to come into the band. I didn't come in with no big name. It won't do me. But to me, that was a whole lot of money for a kid seventeen years old. Making that kind of money... I wasn't thinking about going back to Boston. I was making three or four times as much money as my Daddy was making. He couldn't tell me nothin'.

And I damn near sent all of my money back home, trying to prove to them how good I'm doing in New York! Because I didn't want them to worry. I didn't want my parents to worry about me. "New York City! Oh, that's a terrible place," this, that and the other. "And when you go there, don't look up in the air. Don't look up in the air." I guess somebody was supposed to knock me in the head or something when you look up in the air.

There were so many tales out about New York, and I didn't find it nothin' like I was told. I was having a ball over here, believe me. And I was meeting so many fine people, and going in all of these different places and things. As long you got a pocket-full of money, which is what I had... I don't think my room rent cost over four dollars a week for a room.
